HOME SCIENCE MARCH — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Glucose and oxygen

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Yeast Products? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Yeast Products.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Yeast Products.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Yeast Products.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Yeast Products.

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.

   D. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection 2.3 Special Treatment in Laundry Work 2.4 Ventilation and Li.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection? (1 mark)

   B. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Consumer Protection.

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Paper burning to ash

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Careers in Food and Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Careers in Food and Nutrition.

   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Careers in Food and Nutrition.

8. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pastry Making? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pastry Making.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pastry Making.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Pastry Making.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pastry Making.

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

13. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Producers
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Primary consumers only

14. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C

16. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

17. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Convenience Foods? (1 mark)

   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
